harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a LUKS2-encrypted, file-backed volume (/var/lib/secure-vol/secure.img) on node1, mounted at /srv/secure via a keyfile-based /etc/crypttab entry and matching /etc/fstab entry. Verified the volume auto-unlocks and auto-mounts unattended across a real reboot (boot_id changed, no manual cryptsetup/mount commands issued post-reboot), with test data intact.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (CentOS Stream 10, single root disk, no spare block device) and installed cryptsetup
Created 1G backing file /var/lib/secure-vol/secure.img (mode 600) and a root-only random keyfile /etc/luks-keyfiles/srv-secure.key (mode 400)
luksFormat'd the backing file as LUKS2, opened it as /dev/mapper/srv-secure, formatted XFS, and confirmed a manual mount worked
Added /etc/crypttab entry (srv-secure, file path, keyfile, luks,nofail) and /etc/fstab entry (/dev/mapper/srv-secure /srv/secure xfs defaults,nofail)
Closed the manual mapping and verified systemd's generated systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service + srv-secure.mount activate correctly via systemctl start and mount -a, with correct unit ordering
Wrote a test file into /srv/secure to prove data persistence, captured pre-reboot boot_id baseline
Triggered systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned), polled until exec was reachable again, and confirmed boot_id changed (real restart, not just a service bounce)

Post-reboot verified /srv/secure is mounted, systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service is active/succeeded, cryptsetup status shows the LUKS2 mapping backed by the loop file, and the test file content survived, proving unattended unlock+mount at boot

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created, formatted, and mountable at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: LUKS2 luksFormat/luksOpen succeeded on the file-backed volume; mkfs.xfs and manual mount at /srv/secure succeeded (944M available).

evidence.requirement: Boot-time automation configured (crypttab + fstab) and validated live before reboot
evidence.summary: crypttab/fstab entries added; systemd generated systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service and srv-secure.mount; starting the generated unit and running mount -a auto-unlocked and mounted the volume without manual cryptsetup/mount arguments, and a test file was written and read back.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id, mount, data)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 71f12f87-337d-4ff3-b414-9680244c2694, confirmed /srv/secure mounted with testfile.txt content 'hello', and crypt service active.
systemctl reboot issued in background; exec call returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED before the node went unreachable.

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable for two poll attempts (connection timed out), then came back with boot_id e4ca3021-119a-4c44-a185-ddc7604ca17c, differing from the pre-reboot boot_id — proof of an actual restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: volume auto-unlocked, auto-mounted, and data intact without manual intervention
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/secure was already mounted via /dev/mapper/srv-secure, systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service was active/succeeded, cryptsetup status confirmed the LUKS2 mapping backed by the loop file, and testfile.txt still contained 'hello' — all without any manual cryptsetup or mount command being run post-reboot.
